lines.text: The last time Silas Hask rode into Greyhollow, he had twelve Measurers behind him and a writ. This time he had a tired horse and a box of papers.
Lord Lucan. I'd like to defect. Is there a form?
There is now.
Tamsin wouldn't look at him. Ilse looked at nothing else.
After your fire, the Grand Measurer had what was left of the archive sent to my study. I sorted it. I read every page.
The farm records. Thirty years of them. Names, ages, how much aether, how long each one lasted. Some orders are in my own hand. I never once read what I signed.
Then Nell came into the hall, holding one of Tarn's ears, and stopped dead at the sight of the navy coat.
Hask looked at her for a long time. Then the most senior Magister of the Order knelt on the floor of my hall, before a nine-year-old girl.
Child. I believe I signed the paper that took you. I am more sorry than I have words for, and I have a great many words.
Did you know it was cold? Down there?
No. I made very sure I never knew. That was my whole skill.
You owe her more than a kneel, Magister.
I know. I've brought what I have.
He'd brought the records. Every hollow-born the Order had farmed, and every house that wore their rings. Corvin read the list of houses and went pale.
And a warning you won't like. The Heartstone doesn't only feed rings. Its power runs north, along old lines under the ground, all the way to the Pale.
I don't know what it holds. But the Order's oldest maps all say the same thing. If the Stone stops, something in the north stops with it.
That's what the Order always says. Do as we say, or the north will freeze. You said it to me once, about my wards.
I did. I was lying then. I'm not now. I'm aware that doesn't help.
I didn't believe him. A woman was chained to that Stone, and she had known my name. I wasn't leaving her there because of an old map.
He's a liar, Lucan. He always was. But he was never once wrong about stones.
I put it away, the way you put a stone in your pocket to throw later. I should have listened.
One last thing, and then I'll sit wherever you put me. Lord Stane has the King's vanguard. Six thousand men. He marches on Kesting Pass in four days.
Six thousand. Kesting Pass. Four days. I looked at Halvard's banner, and at the rack of Tobin's blades, and did the maths.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and twenty-eight, coming soon.
